check every listed file and repair from the recorded digests
round43_decision_records.rationale: Across 36 source receipts, 127 records list 780 files. Checking them found 190 that did not exist across 16 sources, although no claim locator depended on any of them. Every affected archive was re-fetched and accepted only on a digest match, then re-extracted, which restored all 190 and incidentally exercised the external-artifact policy on 16 sources rather than the 4 spot checks recorded earlier.
round43_decision_records.decision: List every source file under both conventions, the archive member name that the receipt contract records and the repository path where it lives, check the repository paths on every validation run, and repair by digest-verified re-fetch rather than by deleting the entries.
round43_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: A manifest can no longer assert the presence of a file that is absent, and the repair path is the same digest check the provenance policy already relies on; the risk is that repair depends on the upstream service continuing to serve those exact versions, which is the stated limit of that policy.
round43_decision_records.falsifier: If a listed repository path stops resolving and the gate still passes, the manifest check is decorative.

round44_decision_records.question: Does an archive digest show that the committed files are the right bytes?
alternatives: treat the archive digest as sufficient
add per-file digests computed from the current files
compare each committed file with the same member re-extracted from the digest-verified archive
round44_decision_records.rationale: An archive digest proves the archive, not that the file in the repository came out of it. Computing per-file digests from the current files would record what is there rather than verify it, which is self-attestation. Comparing bytes against a re-fetched archive is the only step that separates the two.
round44_decision_records.decision: Verify source evidence at three separately reported levels: the claim locator file digest and excerpt hash, the archive digest before anything is read, and a byte comparison of each committed file with the same archive member.
round44_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: All 169 locators verify and 138 of 138 compared files are byte identical across 27 archives, with a PDF-only record reported as incomplete rather than counted; the risk is that the byte level has been run over four receipt files so far and the rest are unchecked, which the receipt states.
round44_decision_records.falsifier: If a committed source file differs from the archive member it claims to come from, the evidence chain is broken for that source.

round45_decision_records.question: Should byte-level verification cover the whole evidence base or a sample?
alternatives: keep the four-receipt sample and state the coverage
sample randomly and extrapolate
verify every receipt
round45_decision_records.rationale: Misalignment between a claim and its cited evidence is a common failure of model-written reports, and this project generates its own citations, so a sample would leave the untested part exactly where a reader would look. Every receipt was verified instead: 130 archives re-fetched and accepted only on a digest match, 782 files compared byte for byte with their archive members, none differing.
round45_decision_records.decision: Verify every source receipt at byte level rather than sampling, and rename the status of a versioned PDF record from a failure-sounding label to one that states its digest was verified and it has no members to compare.
round45_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: The evidence chain is complete for every committed source file rather than for a sample; the risk is unchanged and stated, that a re-fetch depends on the upstream service still serving those exact versions.
round45_decision_records.falsifier: If any committed source file differs from its archive member on a later run, the chain is broken for that source and the affected claims must be re-checked.

round46_decision_records.question: Should the byte-level source verification run inside the validation gate?
alternatives: run the full byte-level check on every validation
leave it manual and unchecked
run the local level every time and check the recorded network result for staleness
round46_decision_records.rationale: A gate that reaches the network is not deterministic and fails for reasons unrelated to the work, which is how a gate becomes something people switch off. The claim level is entirely local, so it runs every time. The byte level is recorded with the digest of the evidence base it was run against, and the gate fails when that digest no longer matches, which converts a manual check into an enforced obligation without making validation depend on a network.
round46_decision_records.decision: Run claim-level verification on every validation, and require the byte-level receipt to reference the current evidence base, failing as stale otherwise.
round46_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: The evidence chain is enforced continuously without a network dependency, and adding or changing any locator forces the byte level to be re-run; the risk is that staleness is detected rather than prevented, so a stale window exists between changing the evidence base and re-running the network check.
round46_decision_records.falsifier: If the evidence base can change while the gate still reports the byte-level result as current, the staleness contract is not enforced.

round47_decision_records.question: How should the staleness window be closed without turning the closing command into a rubber stamp?
alternatives: let the loop re-anchor after any run
re-anchor manually and rely on discipline
re-anchor only when verification actually passed, and leave the anchor stale otherwise
round47_decision_records.rationale: A command that re-anchors regardless of the result would silence the gate it exists to satisfy, and evidence that the wiring between checker and fixer can change what a checker reports is a reason to keep that boundary explicit. The anchor is therefore updated only when the claim level passed, every archive reached an acceptable status, and no file mismatched.
round47_decision_records.decision: Close the evidence cycle with a command that re-runs verification and updates the recorded anchor only on a full pass, leaving it stale on any failure, and complete the one record that blocked a pass rather than widening what counts as acceptable.
round47_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: The window closes in the cycle that opens it, held by nine fixtures and five caught mutations including four negative cases where the anchor must not move; the risk is that the command and the gate share an author, so the negative tests are the only thing separating closure from silencing.
round47_decision_records.falsifier: If the anchor updates after a failed verification, the command is a rubber stamp and the staleness contract is void.

round48_decision_records.question: The confirmatory block has no unburned tasks. Where do new ones come from?
alternatives: reuse the variance-block tasks
generate synthetic design questions
build new tasks from recent source studies whose design is withheld, with anchors frozen before any artifact exists
round48_decision_records.rationale: Every existing task is either burned as development data or already consumed by the variance block, so reusing them would score a design the same system has already seen. Two recent studies with clear experimental designs were turned into tasks whose withheld target is the study design itself, and the anchors were written before any candidate artifact existed.
round48_decision_records.decision: Build two new confirmation tasks from unseen recent studies, freeze their anchors before any artifact exists, and check every anchor cue against the released instructions so the task cannot hand the agent its own answer.
round48_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: The confirmatory block has tasks disjoint from all burned ones with anchors that cannot be fitted to outputs; the risk is that two tasks is a small confirmation set, and that a model may have memorised a recent study, which the withheld design and the cue check reduce but do not eliminate.
round48_decision_records.falsifier: If an anchor cue appears in the released instructions, the task hands over part of its own answer and its coverage is inflated.

round49_decision_records.question: What may be reported from the first admissible block?
alternatives: report the condition differences seen in eight episodes
report nothing until the full block runs
report execution, admission and integrity, and refuse to interpret the condition pattern
round49_decision_records.rationale: Eight episodes gave the first data in this project that satisfies the admission rule, with usage measured, transcripts complete, no canary leak and no fabrication redline. They also show a visible pattern in structural gaps across conditions. Two observations per condition cannot separate a condition from a task, and a study that tested a mechanism where it ships found no detectable change despite earlier reports of large gains, which is the standard this block does not meet.
round49_decision_records.decision: Report execution, admission and integrity from this block, record the structural gap counts in the receipt without interpretation, and estimate no treatment effect.
round49_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: The project now has admissible episodes and a working confirmatory pipeline; the risk is that the recorded pattern invites a causal reading, which the receipt refuses explicitly rather than by omission.
round49_decision_records.falsifier: If any of these episodes is later found to violate a declared ceiling or to have an incomplete transcript, its admission was wrong and it must be excluded.

round50_decision_records.question: A declared ceiling refused one episode, and it fell in the most expensive condition. What follows?
alternatives: raise the ceiling so the refusal disappears
drop the refused episode and analyse the rest
treat the violation as an outcome and report the refusal rate per condition
round50_decision_records.rationale: The single refusal fell in the full condition, which uses the most calls in every observation, so a binding ceiling removes episodes non-randomly and dropping them would bias a comparison toward the cheaper condition. Raising the ceiling would hide the asymmetry the measurement just revealed. If the full condition needs more calls, capping calls is the budget match rather than an instrumentation accident, and the endpoint is completion within budget.
round50_decision_records.decision: Treat a ceiling violation as an outcome rather than as data loss, report the refusal rate per condition as part of the design, and leave the ceiling where measurement placed it.
round50_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: The comparison stays budget-matched and the asymmetry is visible instead of removed; the risk is that the admissible set is now unbalanced, so variance components cannot be computed from it, which the guard enforces rather than papers over.
round50_decision_records.falsifier: If refusals occur at similar rates across conditions in a larger block, the asymmetry is not real and treating violation as an outcome adds nothing.

round51_decision_records.question: A declared ceiling refused an episode. Should budget failure be analysed or only logged?
alternatives: log refusals in receipts only
exclude refused episodes and analyse the remainder
declare budget completion as a secondary outcome reported beside the quality endpoint
round51_decision_records.rationale: A refused episode is not missing data: it failed to complete within the budget every condition was given, and refusals fell entirely in the most expensive condition. Reporting only the quality endpoint over survivors would credit a condition for the episodes it completed while hiding the ones it could not.
round51_decision_records.decision: Declare budget completion rate as a secondary outcome computed by the same admission path, report it beside the quality endpoint with denominators stated, never merge the two, and do not adjust a ceiling to remove refusals.
round51_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: A condition that reaches better designs by spending more can no longer look uniformly better, because the cost of that spending appears as its own outcome; the risk is that this outcome was declared after the first refusal was seen, which is recorded rather than concealed and is fixed now so later blocks cannot select it.
round51_decision_records.falsifier: If refusal rates are similar across conditions in a larger block, this outcome adds nothing and the asymmetry seen here was noise.

round52_decision_records.question: How should the budget completion rates be reported given four episodes per condition?
alternatives: report the rates alone
omit them until a larger block exists
report them with denominators and intervals and state what four episodes cannot show
round52_decision_records.rationale: The only refusal fell in the full condition, which is suggestive and unproven. Every Wilson interval on four episodes spans more than half the range, the widest is 0.653 wide, and all four overlap, so the block can show that a ceiling bound and where, but not that completion differs by condition. Small screening blocks read as settled questions can produce worse decisions than no block at all.
round52_decision_records.decision: Report budget completion per condition with completed counts, denominators and Wilson intervals, state that four episodes per condition cannot establish a difference, and keep the outcome separate from the quality endpoint.
round52_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: A reader sees both the asymmetry and its uncertainty; the risk is that a single refusal in the most expensive condition reads as an effect, which the interval widths and the explicit statement are there to prevent.
round52_decision_records.falsifier: If a larger block shows overlapping completion rates across conditions, the asymmetry here was noise and the emphasis was misplaced.

round53_decision_records.question: Should the block be extended now, or should the requirement be recorded first?
alternatives: run a third repeat because it is cheap
run the full 116-episode block
compute the requirement from measured cost and put the spend to the user with a default of not spending
round53_decision_records.rationale: A third repeat would cost about one dollar and move the half width from 0.327 to roughly 0.29, which changes nothing that can be concluded, so it would buy the appearance of progress. Reaching a half width of 0.15 at the lowest observed rate needs 29 episodes per condition, 116 in total, at a measured cost of about 18 dollars, which is six times everything this project has spent on model calls so far.
round53_decision_records.decision: Record the requirement as committed code that reads its cost from an executed receipt rather than from an assumption, do not spend six times the prior total without approval, and ask the question with a default of not spending while the loop continues.
round53_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: The design now states what a decisive block costs instead of drifting toward it in small steps; the risk is that the completion comparison stays uninformative until that block is approved, which the paper already says.
round53_decision_records.falsifier: If a much smaller extension would reach the target precision, the requirement is overstated and the recommendation is wrong.

round54_decision_records.question: Can the quality endpoint be sized, and if not, what should be reported instead?
alternatives: size it using the provisional variance
assume a plausible variance
report that it cannot be sized and name what blocks it
round54_decision_records.rationale: A block size resting on a variance the design cannot yield would look like a plan and function as a guess. The check finds two blockers: no human-anchored labels exist, so judged scoring is inadmissible, and the ceiling refusal left the admissible set unbalanced, so expected mean squares do not apply. The first is an external input that no execution in this loop can supply.
round54_decision_records.decision: Report that the quality endpoint cannot be sized today, name both blockers with their kinds, and record that the calibration labels are the single binding constraint on the quality arm.
round54_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: A reader sees which half of the plan is executable and why the other half is not; the risk is that naming a human dependency can read as an excuse, which the completion arm answers by being planned, costed and executable now.
round54_decision_records.falsifier: If the quality endpoint can be sized from admissible data without human labels, the blocker is misidentified.

round55_decision_records.question: Should the completion arm be pre-registered now, and what should the document fix?
alternatives: analyse the completion arm when the data arrive
write a loose plan
freeze a full preregistration and gate it so it cannot change once the block grows
round55_decision_records.rationale: The completion arm is the only outcome that can be sized and run today, so it is the only one that can be honestly pre-registered. The document fixes the hypothesis without taking a direction from the pilot, the test and alpha, the size and its source, an exclusion rule that forbids removing an episode for its outcome, a stopping rule with no interim looks, the falsifier, and what the arm cannot show.
round55_decision_records.decision: Freeze a preregistration for the completion arm before any episode beyond the current sixteen exists, seal it by its own digest, and gate it so the document cannot change once the block grows.
round55_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: The analysis is fixed before the data that would tempt it, and three failing-first mutations confirm the gate; the risk is that a document written by the agent that will run and analyse the block constrains the analysis without making it independent, which the receipt states rather than implies.
round55_decision_records.falsifier: if the document can be edited after the block grows without the gate firing, the seal is decorative.

round56_decision_records.question: Do the judge reliability figures fall under the same downgrade as the variance components?
alternatives: downgrade them too, since they use the same episodes
leave the distinction implicit
state the distinction explicitly and keep them undowngraded
round56_decision_records.rationale: An audit of every number derived from the pilot and variance blocks found two occurrences without language marking the dependency, both judge reliability figures. They do not need a downgrade for a different reason than the variance components: the admission rule refuses to score an episode whose usage was never measured, and reliability characterises the instrument rather than scoring the episode. Without that stated, a reader cannot tell why one set is provisional and the other is not.
round56_decision_records.decision: Keep the reliability figures undowngraded, and state in the manuscript that they characterise the judge rather than the episodes, naming the admission refusal they fall under.
round56_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: A reader can distinguish instrument characterisation from episode scoring without inferring it; the risk is that the distinction can be stretched to justify keeping other numbers, which is why it is tied to a specific property, whether a verdict reproduces on the same item.
round56_decision_records.falsifier: If a reliability figure is used anywhere as an episode score or as evidence about a condition, the distinction is being abused and the figure must be downgraded.

round57_decision_records.question: Does the reliability measured on the variance block transfer to the new tasks?
alternatives: assume it transfers
re-measure only the high band
judge every element on the new artifacts with both judges and report the stratification
round57_decision_records.rationale: Reliability is a property of an instrument on material, not of the instrument alone, so it had to be re-measured on tasks the instrument had never seen. Raw agreement fell to 0.667 from 0.703, but six items produced an unparsed verdict from one judge and are counted as disagreements; excluding those, agreement was 0.788 with kappa 0.492, above the earlier figures. The stratification replicated exactly: twelve of twelve above 0.9, fourteen of eighteen in the middle, zero of nine below 0.7.
round57_decision_records.decision: Report the replication with unparsed verdicts counted as disagreements, state both the raw and the excluding figures, and treat the replicated stratification as support for the confidence floor rather than for the judge in general.
round57_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: The part of the instrument actually used is now shown to hold on unseen tasks; the risk is that both judges share the same prompt and span retrieval, so a shared retrieval failure would look like agreement, which is recorded as a limit.
round57_decision_records.falsifier: If a later block shows disagreement among high-confidence pairs, the floor does not hold and the abstention rule must be raised or abandoned.

round58_decision_records.question: Is the candidate filter high-recall, as the endpoint design assumes?
alternatives: assume the filter rarely misses
check only items where a span was retrieved
re-judge every no-span item on the full artifact
round58_decision_records.rationale: The endpoint is filter plus verification, and the filter was demoted to a high-recall candidate step on the assumption that it rarely misses. Nine items returned no span and were scored negative without any model call. Shown the full artifact, both judges call four of those nine satisfied, and at least one calls five. The agreement on those items was a shared retrieval failure rather than a judgement.
round58_decision_records.decision: Record the high-recall assumption as falsified, treat a no-span result as an unresolved item rather than a negative verdict, and require the retrieval step to have measured recall before the endpoint is used for scoring.
round58_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: A silent miss can no longer be scored as a negative, which removes a source of understated coverage; the risk is that this measures only items where retrieval returned nothing, and items with a poor span could fail the same way without being visible.
round58_decision_records.falsifier: If a measured recall check shows the filter misses rarely on a larger sample, the assumption stands and this result was specific to nine items.

round59_decision_records.question: Does the retrieval failure extend to items where a span was returned?
alternatives: assume a returned span is adequate
check only a sample
re-judge every span-negative item on the full artifact
round59_decision_records.rationale: The previous cycle measured only items where retrieval returned nothing, leaving the larger failure mode untested. Of nine items where a span was returned and judged negative, three are called satisfied by both models on the full artifact. Combined with the no-span items, seven of eighteen pipeline negatives are overturned, and the rates are similar at four of nine and three of nine, so a returned span is not protection.
round59_decision_records.decision: Report the complete negative-overturn rate with its split, state that the endpoint understates coverage in one direction at roughly that rate, and bound the whole measurement by noting that the reference is two-judge agreement on the full artifact rather than ground truth.
round59_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: The size and direction of the endpoint bias are now measured rather than suspected; the risk is that the reference is itself judge-based, so the result shows instability under a wider view rather than establishing the wider view as correct.
round59_decision_records.falsifier: If human labels later agree with the pipeline verdicts on these items, the wider view was wrong and the overturn rate does not indicate bias.

round60_decision_records.question: Should the endpoint repair its retrieval or remove it?
alternatives: widen the cues and re-measure
keep retrieval and accept the miss rate
judge the whole artifact and keep the cheaper verdict on a subsample
round60_decision_records.rationale: Repair is unattractive because the failure is not directional in a way cues can fix: three of four no-span misses were one element stated in wording the cues do not match, and poor spans fail at a similar rate, so widening cues trades one silent miss for another. Measured cost makes removal affordable, at 1.61 times per judgement, and the full-artifact path has no retrieval stage to miss anything.
round60_decision_records.decision: Judge the whole artifact as the primary path, retain the span-based verdict on a twenty percent subsample as a drift check, and do not repair cue retrieval.
round60_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: A measured and directional failure mode is removed for about a sixty percent cost increase per judgement; the risk is that full-artifact judging has no accuracy measurement of its own, so an unmeasured failure mode replaces a measured one, and the subsample exists to make disagreement visible rather than assumed away.
round60_decision_records.falsifier: If the subsample shows the two paths agreeing closely, the retrieval stage was not the problem and the extra cost is unjustified.

round61_decision_records.question: What does the endpoint read once retrieval is removed, and how should it be reported?
alternatives: report per-condition coverage under the new method
report nothing until calibration
report the aggregate instrument shift and compare it with the detectable effect
round61_decision_records.rationale: Judging the whole artifact raises mean coverage from 0.542 to 0.729, a shift of 0.188, with seventeen of forty-eight verdicts changing and four moving toward negative rather than away, so the change is not simply a looser rule. The paired minimum detectable effect on this endpoint is 0.0825, so the method choice moves the reading by about 2.3 times the smallest effect the design was sized to detect.
round61_decision_records.decision: Report the aggregate instrument shift and its ratio to the detectable effect, do not report per-condition coverage under the new method, and restate that these verdicts remain inadmissible for scoring.
round61_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: The paper can show that an instrument choice dominates the comparison it serves, which is the thesis argument made quantitative; the risk is that a reader takes the coverage figures as outcomes, which the refusal to break them out by condition and the admissibility statement are there to prevent.
round61_decision_records.falsifier: If a calibrated endpoint shows the two methods reading within the detectable effect of each other, the method choice does not dominate and this comparison is overstated.

round62_decision_records.question: Can the paired detectable effect still size a block once the instrument varies?
alternatives: keep the number and note the caveat
adjust it by the mean method shift
void it as a design target and require the instrument to enter the variance model
round62_decision_records.rationale: The instrument does not merely shift the endpoint. Across the eight artifacts the method difference has a standard deviation of 0.301, about 3.65 times the detectable effect the design was sized for, and its variance is 1.48 times the variance of the coverage being measured. The difference also changes sign, from minus 0.167 to plus 0.667, so no constant adjustment recovers the earlier number.
round62_decision_records.decision: Void the paired minimum detectable effect as a design target, record that it omitted a variance component larger than the one it used, and require sample-size planning to treat the scoring method as a facet with its own variance rather than as a settled choice.
round62_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: The design can no longer be sized on a number that ignores its largest source of variation; the risk is that the instrument facet is estimated here from eight artifacts with one judge, so the replacement plan needs its own measurement before it can be trusted.
round62_decision_records.falsifier: If a larger sample shows the method difference small and consistent, the instrument is close to fixed and the earlier detectable effect stands.

round63_decision_records.question: With the scoring method as a facet, can the quality arm be sized at all?
alternatives: size a larger block on the new variance model
pool the two tasks to gain degrees of freedom
report that the endpoint does not separate conditions and stop sizing it
round63_decision_records.rationale: A crossed condition by method by element study per task puts 0.9 percent of the clamped variance on the condition in one task and a negative estimate clamping to zero in the other, against 47.9 percent element and 37.1 percent residual in the first and 50.5 percent residual in the second. Dependability as run is 0.040 and 0.000, and no element count within the cap reaches 0.8, because more measurement cannot enlarge a signal estimated at zero. Pooling tasks was rejected because the anchor elements are task specific, so pooling would manufacture degrees of freedom by pretending different elements are the same facet.
round63_decision_records.decision: Stop sizing the quality arm. Report that the endpoint as constructed does not separate the conditions it was built to compare, that adding episodes cannot repair this, and that either the endpoint changes or no condition claim is available from it.
round63_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: The project stops planning spend on a comparison the instrument cannot make, which is the honest outcome; the risk is that four conditions leave the condition component only three degrees of freedom, so a near-zero estimate could reflect sampling error rather than a genuinely absent signal, and the negative components say exactly that.
round63_decision_records.falsifier: If an endpoint with the same conditions and more artifacts shows a condition component that is a material share of variance, the endpoint separates conditions and this conclusion was an artefact of eight artifacts.

round64_decision_records.question: Is the endpoint insensitive, or are the conditions inert?
alternatives: treat the null as evidence the conditions do not matter
switch the primary endpoint to a process quantity
report the contrast and name the ambiguity as unresolved by this design
round64_decision_records.rationale: Process quantities separate the conditions sharply, with interface calls at 0.899 and 0.951 and context tokens at 0.915 and 0.925, while artifact size separates weakly at 0.367 and 0.702 and judged coverage not at all. The process figures are close to definitional, since a condition supplying more context and access makes more calls by construction, so they check that the manipulation took effect rather than measure an effect on quality. Switching the primary endpoint to a process quantity was rejected for exactly that reason: it would report the manipulation back as if it were a result.
round64_decision_records.decision: Report the contrast, treat the process figures as a manipulation check, and state that the design cannot distinguish an inert manipulation from an insensitive endpoint, while noting that the falsified retrieval filter and the near-zero condition component both point at the endpoint.
round64_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: The paper avoids the two available errors, which are declaring a null result and promoting a definitional quantity to an outcome; the risk is that the ambiguity is left standing, which is the honest state given fifteen admissible episodes.
round64_decision_records.falsifier: If a repaired endpoint on the same artifacts shows a material condition component, the endpoint was insensitive and the null reading was wrong.

round65_decision_records.question: Does repairing the endpoint reveal the condition effect it was suspected of hiding?
alternatives: declare a null effect of the conditions
keep both readings open indefinitely
report that repair did not produce the component and say which reading that favours
round65_decision_records.rationale: The endpoint was rebuilt without the falsified retrieval stage and with a genuine second repeat, so within-cell variation estimates error directly. The condition share is 0.026 and a clamped zero, against 0.009 and zero before. The component did not appear, which addresses the insensitive-endpoint reading on its own terms and weakens it.

round84_decision_records.question: receipt가 "이 숫자는 불변 실험 노드의 실행에서 나왔다"를 어떻게 증명하게 할 것인가?
alternatives: receipt가 run id를 자기 신고하면 신뢰
run id 필드만 필수로 요구하고 존재는 확인하지 않음
run 저장소에서 존재·상태 done·커밋 일치를 게이트가 직접 재확인
round84_decision_records.rationale: 자기 신고 필드를 검사하는 게이트는 검사가 아니라 주석이다. RD-80A가 만든 출처 게이트는 origin·usage·transcript 축을 검사했지만 "그 실행이 실제로 불변 노드 안에서 일어났는가"는 묻지 못했다. run id를 요구만 하고 조회하지 않으면 아무 문자열이나 통과한다. 게이트는 로컬 run 저장소에서 run을 직접 조회해 존재·상태·커밋을 재도출해야 한다.
round84_decision_records.decision: 실행을 주장하는 non-legacy receipt에 orx_project_id·orx_experiment_id·orx_run_id·node_commit을 필수화하고, 게이트가 run 저장소에서 run 존재·status=done·node_commit 일치를 확인한다. 저장소를 못 읽으면 검증 불가로 실패시킨다(fail-closed).
round84_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: 효과: 기판 밖에서 실행된 에피소드가 결과로 들어올 수 없다. 위험: run 저장소가 없는 환경에서 정당한 receipt도 막힌다 — 검증 불가를 통과로 바꾸지 않는 것이 의도된 선택이다.
round84_decision_records.falsifier: 존재하지 않는 run id나 done이 아닌 run을 가진 receipt가 통과하면 이 결정은 실패한 것이다.

round85_decision_records.question: 실행되지 않은 Study B를 원고에 어떻게 넣을 것인가?
alternatives: 실행될 때까지 원고에서 빼둔다
설계를 서술하되 결과 칸을 비워둔다
결과 칸에 "미실행"을 명시한 표를 넣고 설계 값과 관측을 분리한다
round85_decision_records.rationale: 빼두면 논문의 주 기여가 보이지 않고, 결과 칸을 그냥 비우면 누락과 구별되지 않는다. 0013 §3은 Study A를 측정 장으로, Study B를 주 장으로 재배치하되 결과표에 "미실행"을 표기하라고 지시한다. MDE와 단가는 각각 라벨된 검정력 계산과 실측 receipt에서 오므로 설계 값으로 분리해 적는다.
round85_decision_records.decision: Ⅲ장 8절에 메커니즘·아암·주 대비·풀링을 서술하고, Ⅳ장 12절에 아암별 상태표를 넣되 검증기 통과율 열을 전부 "미실행"으로 채운다. Ⅳ장 첫머리에 이 장이 측정 장임을 선언한다. 표는 그래프의 mechanism 노드와 사전등록 문서를 읽어 assert로 검증한다.
round85_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: 효과: 미실행이 누락이 아니라 기록이 된다. 위험: 설계 값을 결과로 오독할 수 있어 "설계 파라미터이지 관측이 아니다"를 본문에 명시했다.
round85_decision_records.falsifier: 실행되지 않은 아암의 칸에 숫자가 들어가면 이 결정은 실패한 것이다.

round86_decision_records.question: Q-0009 시나리오 (a) 원안이 확정된 뒤 봉인과 실행을 어떻게 진행하는가?
alternatives: 봉인 없이 바로 실행
상한 재확인을 다시 요구
0014a 확정대로 봉인 후 드라이런·실행
round86_decision_records.rationale: 사용자가 10:47 KST에 시나리오 (a) 원안을 확정했다: 3아암 × 3과제 × n=40 = 360 에피소드, 상한 $48.47, 모델 claude-haiku-4-5 고정. 0014 §2의 봉인 보류를 해제한다. 승인 범위는 사전등록 §2~§6을 봉인 직전까지 확정한 값과 정확히 일치한다. 봉인 후 §2~§6 수정 금지, 중간 확인 금지, 결과 기반 에피소드 제외 금지.
round86_decision_records.decision: (1) Q-0009 상태를 APPROVED (a) 확정으로 갱신하고 승인 기록 파일을 만든다. (2) 미완 항목 폐쇄를 문서에 반영하고 사전등록을 sha256으로 봉인한다. (3) 아암 커밋 해시를 확정하고 failing-first를 통과시킨 뒤 드라이런을, 그 다음 orx 노드로 스크리닝을 실행한다.
round86_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: 효과: 승인된 범위 안에서 1차 스크리닝을 완결한다. 위험: 상한에 근접하면 실행을 멈춰야 하고 그 사실은 예산 완주율 endpoint에 경쟁 사건으로 반영된다.
round86_decision_records.falsifier: 봉인된 §2~§6이 실행 중 수정되거나, 상한을 넘겨 지출이 이루어지면 이 결정은 실패한 것이다.
